chunks: And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
If the sins of a believer were as much as the sand of the desert or the froth of the sea, Allah would forgive them for him; so do not become bold (in sinning).
ai.seo_question: How many sins can Allah forgive a believer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) uses hyperbolic imagery of 'sand of the desert' and 'sea froth' to emphasize the boundless nature of divine forgiveness for believers, a concept central to Shia theology regarding the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt and the efficacy of repentance. This narration, found in *Kitab al-Mumin*, serves as a balanced exhortation: it encourages hope in Allah’s mercy while warning against *istikhfaf* (underestimating the gravity of sin) or becoming presumptuous (*tajarru*) due to that same mercy.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 64. It has been reported that Abu Ja'far (a.s) said:
If the sins of a believer were as much as the sand in the desert or the froth of the sea, Allah would forgive them all; but do not become bold (in sinning, mistaking His Mercy for weakness).
